board.review.tip.description: Tooltip on a card's reviewer line: who is reviewing it, since when ({ago}: "5 min ago").

board.review.tipNotRunning.defaultMessage: {agent} started reviewing it {ago}, and isn't running.
board.review.tipNotRunning.description: Tooltip on a card's reviewer line, in amber: the reviewer ({agent}) started {ago} ("5 min ago") but its session isn't running now.

board.review.tipRemoved.defaultMessage: {agent} started reviewing it {ago}, and was removed.
board.review.tipRemoved.description: Tooltip on a card's reviewer line, in amber: the reviewer ({agent}) started {ago} ("5 min ago") and was removed from the project since.

board.reviewSkip.askMessage.defaultMessage: Submitting it will finish it with no review: a code card goes on to its merge, with its merge checks. The card shows Review skipped, with your note.
board.reviewSkip.askMessage.description: The question before a card is set to skip its review (#1625): what that means. Review skipped is the mark's text.

board.reviewSkip.askTitle.description: Title of the question before a card is set to skip its review (#1625). {card} is the card's name.

board.reviewSkip.change.description: A button beside a card's Review field in its dialog (#1625): Skip Review… makes it skip its review (asking why, optional), Review It sets it back to be reviewed. Select keys: whether it skips review now.

board.reviewSkip.confirm.description: A button on the banner of a card an agent proposed should skip its review (#1625): makes it skip review.

board.reviewSkip.confirmLabel.description: The button of the question before a card is set to skip its review (#1625).

board.reviewSkip.failed.defaultMessage: Whether the card skips review wasn't changed
board.reviewSkip.failed.description: An error toast's title (#1625): setting whether a card skips its review failed. Its text says why.

board.reviewSkip.field.description: A field label in the card dialog (#1625): whether the card is reviewed as its project's rules say, or skips its review.

board.reviewSkip.keep.description: A button on the banner of a card an agent proposed should skip its review (#1625): keeps its review.

board.reviewSkip.newChoice.description: A tick box in the New Card dialog (#1625): the card skips its review; submitting it finishes it (a code card still goes on to its merge, with its merge checks).

board.reviewSkip.note.description: Placeholder of the box beside the New Card dialog's Skip review tick box (#1625): the user's note on why the card skips review.

board.reviewSkip.proposal.defaultMessage: Skip review? The agent that made this card proposes it: {reason}
board.reviewSkip.proposal.description: A banner in a card's dialog (#1625): the agent that made the card proposed that it skip its review, with its reason ({reason}: the agent's words); the user decides.

board.reviewSkip.proposedMark.description: A dashed mark on a card's tile (#1625): the agent that made it proposed that it skip its review, not answered yet.

board.reviewSkip.proposedTip.defaultMessage: Skip review? Proposed by the agent that made it: open the card to decide.
board.reviewSkip.proposedTip.description: Tooltip and accessible name of a card's mark when the agent that made it proposed that it skip its review and nobody has answered yet (#1625).

board.reviewSkip.reason.description: The label of the field in the question before a card is set to skip its review (#1625): the user's note on why.

board.reviewSkip.reviewed.description: The card dialog's Review field (#1625): the card is reviewed as its project's rules say.

board.reviewSkip.skipped.description: A mark on a card's tile (#1625): the card skips its review; its submission finishes it (a code card still goes on to its merge).

board.reviewSkip.skippedTip.defaultMessage: {who, select, assistant {Review skipped, set by the Assistant: {reason}} note {Review skipped, set by you: {reason}} other {Review skipped, set by you.}}
board.reviewSkip.skippedTip.description: Tooltip and accessible name of a card's Review skipped mark (#1625): who set it and why. Select keys (keep them): assistant, the Combwork Assistant set it, with the user's reason ({reason}: their words); note, the user set it with a note ({reason}); other, the user set it with no note.

board.reviewSkip.working.description: A button while whether the card skips review is being saved (#1625).

board.run.agentStopped.defaultMessage: Its agent stopped before it finished
board.run.agentStopped.description: A run's status line in the Progress panel: the agent that ran it stopped first.

board.run.failedAfter.description: A failed run's status line in the Progress panel. {took} is how long it ran ("4 min").

board.run.finishing.description: A running run's status line in the Progress panel, just past its estimate. {took} is how long it has run ("3 min").

board.run.goneAfter.description: A run's status line in the Progress panel: its process ended without saying how it went. {took} is how long it ran ("4 min").

board.run.overEstimate.description: A running run's status line in the Progress panel, well past its estimate. {took} is how long it has run ("3 min").

board.run.passedIn.description: A finished run's status line in the Progress panel. {took} is how long it took ("4 min").

board.run.ranThenWaiting.description: A run's status line in the Progress panel: it ran for {took}, then has been waiting (for a test slot, say) for {waited}. Both are durations ("3 min").

board.run.staleFor.description: A run's status line in the Progress panel: no news from it for a while. {ago} is how long ("12 min").

board.run.state.defaultMessage: {state, select, running {running} failed {failed} stale {stopped reporting} passed {passed} stopped {stopped} gone {ended without a report} other {{state}}}
board.run.state.description: A Progress panel run's state in a few words, lower case: in a hover ("Copy the summary (failed)") and a run's accessible name. stale: it stopped reporting; gone: its process ended without saying how it went.

board.run.stoppedAfter.description: A run's status line in the Progress panel: its command was interrupted. {took} is how long it ran ("4 min").

board.run.timeLeft.description: A running run's status line in the Progress panel: how long it has run ({took}) and about how long it has left ({left}). Both are durations ("3 min").

board.run.waiting.description: A run's status line in the Progress panel: it has been waiting (for a test slot, say) for {waited} ("3 min"). Lower case, as the line may follow a duration.

board.run.wordsStale.description: A run in a few words, for an agent's status line: {run} is its title and steps ("e2e 4/12"); it stopped reporting.

board.run.wordsWaiting.description: A run in a few words, for an agent's status line: {run} is its title and steps ("e2e 4/12"); it is waiting (for a test slot, say).

board.runs.agent.description: Accessible name of the Progress panel's Runs tab filter by agent: only the runs one agent ran.

board.runs.anyAgent.description: A choice of the Progress panel's Runs tab filter by agent: runs of every agent.

board.runs.anyLane.description: A choice of the Progress panel's Runs tab filter by lane: runs of any card.

board.runs.cardRun.description: A run named with its card in the Progress panel's Runs tab: the card's name ({card}: its key, such as AL-12) and the run's title ({run}).

board.runs.cardSummary.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {# run} other {# runs}} · {failed, plural, =0 {{stopped, plural, =0 {all passed} other {# stopped}}} other {# failed}}{running, select, yes { · running} other {}}
board.runs.cardSummary.description: The summary on a card's heading in the Progress panel's Runs tab, where runs are grouped by card: how many runs it had that day ({n}), how many failed ({failed}), else how many stopped without passing or failing ({stopped}), else all passed; then " · running" while one of its runs is still going. Keep the select keys.

board.runs.clear.description: A button in the Progress panel's Runs tab: clears its filters and search.

board.runs.dockEdge.description: Accessible name of the handle on the top edge of the Progress panel's Runs tab's finished runs (docked at the bottom): drag it to make them taller or shorter.

board.runs.dockEdgeTip.defaultMessage: Drag to make the finished runs taller or shorter; double-click for {rows, plural, one {# lane row} other {# lane rows}}
board.runs.dockEdgeTip.description: Tooltip of the handle on the top edge of the Progress panel's Runs tab's finished runs. {rows} is their default height in the Pulse tab's lane rows (6.5).

board.runs.dockEdgeValue.defaultMessage: {rows, plural, one {# lane row high} other {# lane rows high}}
board.runs.dockEdgeValue.description: The value of the handle on the top edge of the Progress panel's Runs tab's finished runs, for screen readers: how tall they are, in the height of the Pulse tab's lane rows ({rows}, may be a fraction such as 6.5).

board.runs.failedOnly.description: A toggle in the Progress panel's Runs tab: shows only the runs that failed.

board.runs.finished.description: Accessible name of the Progress panel's Runs tab's finished runs, docked at the bottom (Today, then older days).

board.runs.group.defaultMessage: {what} ×{n, number} · {outcome, select, passed {{failed, plural, =0 {all passed} one {# failed, then passed} other {# failed, then passed}}} failed {{failed, plural, one {# failed} other {# failed}}} other {{failed, plural, =0 {last stopped} one {# failed, last stopped} other {# failed, last stopped}}}}
board.runs.group.description: A line in the Progress panel's Runs tab for one run tried several times the same day: what ran ({what}: a card and the run's title), how many times ({n}), how many of them failed ({failed}) and how the last one ended (outcome: passed, failed, or stopped without passing or failing). Keep the select keys.

board.runs.lane.description: Accessible name of the Progress panel's Runs tab filter by lane: only the runs for a lane's cards.

board.runs.noFinished.description: The Progress panel's Runs tab's finished runs (docked at the bottom) when Combwork has none.

board.runs.none.defaultMessage: No runs yet. When an agent runs tests or a build with progress reporting, every run shows here, kept by day.
board.runs.none.description: The Progress panel's Runs tab when Combwork has no runs.

board.runs.noneMatch.description: The Progress panel's Runs tab when no run matches its filters or search.

board.runs.noneToday.description: Under Today in the Progress panel's Runs tab's finished runs: no run ended today (older days follow).

board.runs.other.description: The heading of a group in the Progress panel's Runs tab, where runs are grouped by card: the runs for no card (Combwork's own, the user's scripts) follow.

board.runs.queueChecks.description: A line in the Progress panel's Runs tab folding the merge queue's checks for one card: the checks it ran ({checks}: their names, a list such as "lint, typecheck") and how many of its runs failed ({failed}, nothing when none).

board.runs.search.description: Placeholder and accessible name of the search box in the Progress panel's Runs tab: finds runs by title, command, agent or card.

board.runs.today.description: A heading in the Progress panel's Runs tab: the runs that ended today follow.

board.runs.yesterday.description: A heading in the Progress panel's Runs tab: the runs that ended yesterday follow.

board.setAside.add.description: Button: adds the set-aside card to the board as a new card.

board.setAside.added.description: A notification: the set-aside card was added to the board with this number.

board.setAside.adding.description: The Add to Board button while the card is being added.

board.setAside.close.description: Button: closes the dialog listing set-aside cards.

board.setAside.discard.description: Button: discards the set-aside card (asks first). The … says it asks: keep it.

board.setAside.discardButton.description: Button in the confirmation: discards the set-aside card.

board.setAside.discardMessage.defaultMessage: It doesn't reach the board: its file goes to the Recycle Bin{readable, select, yes {, with its comments and history} other {}}.
board.setAside.discardMessage.description: The confirmation before a set-aside card is discarded; readable (yes) when it is a card, not a damaged file. Recycle Bin is Windows' name for it.

board.setAside.discardTitle.description: Title of the confirmation before a set-aside card is discarded. {title} is its title.

board.setAside.discarding.description: The Discard button while the card is being discarded.

board.setAside.intro.defaultMessage: This workspace was opened in an older Combwork, which saved these cards where it keeps them. They were set aside, unchanged, and not added to the board. Add each one, or discard it.
board.setAside.intro.description: The top of the dialog listing cards an older Combwork saved.

board.setAside.keeps.description: Beside a set-aside card: its old number {n} is free on this board, so Add gives it that number.

board.setAside.links.defaultMessage: Nothing is rewritten for them: a card here that links to one by its old number keeps that number, and a card added under a new number keeps its own links as they were.
board.setAside.links.description: A note in the dialog listing cards an older Combwork saved: Combwork changes no references between cards when adding them.

board.setAside.loading.description: The dialog listing cards an older Combwork saved, while it reads them.

board.setAside.made.description: Who made a set-aside card ({by}: a name, You or Assistant) and when ({when}: a date and time).

board.setAside.menu.description: An item of the board's ⋯ menu, shown while cards an older Combwork saved are set aside: opens the dialog to add or discard them. {n} is how many. The … says it opens a dialog: keep it.

board.setAside.none.description: The dialog listing cards an older Combwork saved, when none are left.

board.setAside.number.description: A set-aside card's number as the older Combwork gave it. {n} is the number (after #).

board.setAside.taken.defaultMessage: #{n} is taken here: Add gives the next free number
board.setAside.taken.description: Beside a set-aside card: a card on this board has its old number {n}, so Add gives it a new one.

board.setAside.title.defaultMessage: Cards Made by an Older Combwork
board.setAside.title.description: Title of the dialog listing cards an older version of Combwork saved in this workspace after the board moved to its database; they were kept aside, not added to the board.

board.setAside.unreadable.defaultMessage: This file isn't a card Combwork can read: it can only be discarded.
board.setAside.unreadable.description: A set-aside file that is not a valid card.

board.setAside.where.defaultMessage: {project, select, none {The workspace} other {{project}}} · {column} · {comments, plural, =0 {no comments} one {# comment} other {# comments}}
board.setAside.where.description: A set-aside card's project (a folder name; none: about the whole workspace), its board column, and how many comments it has.

board.slots.agentMerging.description: Who holds the merge slot: an agent ({agent}) merging, then the cards it merges ({cards}: "#305, #306"; none: leave that branch empty).

board.slots.agentNext.defaultMessage: {agent} is next to merge{cards, select, none {} other { {cards}}}
board.slots.agentNext.description: Who holds the merge slot: an agent ({agent}) whose turn it is, not started yet, then the cards it will merge ({cards}: "#305, #306"; none: leave that branch empty).

board.slots.free.description: A merge slot nobody holds, after its branch ("main: free"). Lower case.

board.slots.freeNext.description: A merge slot nobody holds, after its branch ("main: free, B4 next"): the agent next in line ({agent}) gets it. Lower case.

board.slots.held.description: A merge slot in a line, after its branch: who holds it ({holder}: "B4 is merging #305"), how long so far ({sofar}: "3 min") and how long its hold has left ({left}: "57 min").

board.slots.heldOver.description: A merge slot in a line, after its branch: who holds it ({holder}: "B4 is merging #305"), how long so far ({sofar}: "63 min"), and that its hold has run out.

board.slots.into.description: Where a merge goes: into a branch ({branch}, shown as code; keep the <code> tags around it).

board.slots.line.description: A merge slot in the Progress panel: its branch ({name}, shown as code: keep the <branch> tags around it) and who holds it or waits for it ({state}). Your language's punctuation goes around the colon.

board.slots.minutes.description: How long a merge has held the merge slot (or has left), in whole minutes ("48 min"). Keep it short: an abbreviation.

board.slots.note.defaultMessage: {who} into {branch} (the merge slot). Merge waits until it is free{waiting, plural, =0 {} other {; # waiting}}.
board.slots.note.description: The Merge dialog's note while the branch it merges into ({branch}) is taken: who holds it ({who}: "B4 is merging #305"), that the merge waits, and how many wait in line ({waiting}; none: leave that branch empty).

board.slots.release.description: Button on a merge slot: frees the slot from a holder that is stuck. Keep it short.

board.slots.releaseAgent.defaultMessage: {agent} holds the merge slot for {project} · {branch}. Release it only if it is stuck: {agent} may be in the middle of merging, and is told the slot was released when it next asks.
board.slots.releaseAgent.description: The confirmation before freeing a merge slot an agent ({agent}) holds, for a project ({project}) and its branch ({branch}).

board.slots.releaseFailed.description: An error's title: freeing a merge slot failed.

board.slots.releaseNext.defaultMessage: {agent} is next in line and gets it.
board.slots.releaseNext.description: Under the confirmation before freeing a merge slot: the agent next in line ({agent}) gets the slot.

board.slots.releaseTipAgent.defaultMessage: Release the merge slot {agent} holds, if it is stuck
board.slots.releaseTipAgent.description: Tooltip of the Release button on a merge slot an agent ({agent}) holds.

board.slots.releaseTipYou.defaultMessage: Release the merge slot your merge holds, if it is stuck
board.slots.releaseTipYou.description: Tooltip of the Release button on a merge slot the user's own merge holds.

board.slots.releaseTitle.description: Title of the confirmation before freeing a merge slot from its holder.

board.slots.releaseYours.defaultMessage: Your merge holds the merge slot for {project} · {branch}. Release it only if it is stuck: the merge may still be running.
board.slots.releaseYours.description: The confirmation before freeing a merge slot the user's own merge holds, for a project ({project}) and its branch ({branch}).

board.slots.underMinute.description: How long a merge has held the merge slot (or has left), when under a minute. Lower case: it starts a phrase ("under a minute so far").

board.slots.waiting.description: Who waits for the merge slot, in line order ({agents}: their names, listed).

board.slots.waitingToMerge.description: Who has the merge slot in the Merge dialog's note when nobody holds it: the agent first in line ({agent}). It starts the note.

board.slots.youMerging.description: Who holds the merge slot, inside a line ("main: you are merging (3 min so far…)"): the user (merging from the window). Lower case.

board.slots.youMergingStart.description: Who holds the merge slot, at the start of a line: the user (merging from the window).

board.stall.hintFollowUp.defaultMessage: Its builder waits for its reviewer to check the follow-up it posted. Show the reviewer and ask it to answer it.
board.stall.hintFollowUp.description: Tooltip on a card stalled in Review or Passed (#1467): in a card loop, the builder posted a follow-up for its reviewer to check (a change asked of reviewed work, such as a screenshot's), and nobody answered.

board.stall.hintLaneOrder.defaultMessage: Its builder and its lane's reviewer are each waiting for the other. Ask the builder to send the card its reviewer waits for, or ask the reviewer to review this one.
board.stall.hintLaneOrder.description: Tooltip on a card stalled in Review by its card loop's deadlock: the builder sent this card to Review and waits for its verdict, while the loop's reviewer waits for another card of the loop to arrive.

board.stall.hintLoopStep.defaultMessage: Its builder waits for its reviewer to check the design it posted. Ask the reviewer to answer it, or tell the builder to go ahead as posted.
board.stall.hintLoopStep.description: Tooltip on a card stalled in Doing (#1382): in a card loop, the builder posted a design for its reviewer to check before building, and nobody answered.

board.stall.hintNobody.defaultMessage: Nobody is working on it. Start it again (on this agent or another), or move it back to Todo.
board.stall.hintNobody.description: Tooltip on a card stalled in Doing: no agent is working on it. Todo is a board column.

board.stall.hintNotWatching.defaultMessage: Nothing will wake that agent when this card changes. Show it and ask it to carry on its card loop.
board.stall.hintNotWatching.description: Tooltip on a stalled card: an agent in a card loop stopped without a card watch (what wakes it when the card changes).

board.stall.hintReviewSilent.defaultMessage: Its reviewer may have finished its turn without Combwork seeing it end. Show the reviewer: if its terminal waits at its prompt, Mark idle, and the watch wakes it.
board.stall.hintReviewSilent.description: Tooltip on a card stalled in Review whose reviewer Combwork has heard nothing from. "Mark idle" is a command in the agent's menu: keep its wording as that command is translated.

board.stall.hintReviewVerdict.defaultMessage: Its reviewer stopped without a verdict and waits on the card. Read its latest comment (it may have a question for you), then show the reviewer and ask it to finish its review.
board.stall.hintReviewVerdict.description: Tooltip on a card stalled in Review: its reviewer started reviewing, then went back to waiting on the card without passing or failing it.

board.stall.hintReviewWait.defaultMessage: Its reviewer's watch didn't wake it. Show the reviewer and ask it to review the card.
board.stall.hintReviewWait.description: Tooltip on a card stalled in Review: its reviewer watches it but has not started.

board.stall.hintWakeUntaken.defaultMessage: Combwork typed this card's wake into that agent, but its CLI didn't send it. Show the agent, click its terminal and press Enter.
board.stall.hintWakeUntaken.description: Tooltip on a stalled card: Combwork typed the line that wakes the agent into its terminal, and the agent's CLI never sent it (it waits in the agent's prompt).

board.stalled.followUpWait.defaultMessage: {builder} posted a follow-up on {card} for its reviewer to check and has waited {waited}: nobody has answered it.
board.stalled.followUpWait.description: Why a card in Review or Passed is stalled (#1467): in a card loop, its builder ({builder}, an agent's name) posted a follow-up for its reviewer to check (a change asked of reviewed work, such as a screenshot's), and is only waiting; no reviewer answered. {card} is the card’s name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none; {waited} how long ("40 min", "2 h 5 min").

board.stalled.laneOrderWait.defaultMessage: {reviewer} is waiting for {other}, before {card} in the lane, while {builder} waits on the review of {card}: each has waited on the other for {waited}.
board.stalled.laneOrderWait.description: Why a card in Review is stalled: its lane is deadlocked. The lane's reviewer ({reviewer}, an agent's name) waits for another card that comes before this one in the lane ({other}), while the lane's builder ({builder}, an agent's name) waits for this card's verdict. {card} and {other} are cards' names: a key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none; {waited} how long both have been waiting so ("40 min", "2 h 5 min").

board.stalled.loopStepWait.defaultMessage: {builder} posted a design on {card} for its reviewer to check and has waited {waited}: nobody has answered it, and it hasn't gone ahead as posted.
board.stalled.loopStepWait.description: Why a card in Doing is stalled (#1382): in a card loop, its builder ({builder}, an agent's name) posted a design for its reviewer to check before building, and is only waiting; no reviewer answered, and the builder didn't go ahead once its wait (Card loops → Design check wait) was over. {card} is the card’s name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none; {waited} how long ("40 min", "2 h 5 min").

board.stalled.noAgent.defaultMessage: In Active, but no agent has it.
board.stalled.noAgent.description: Why a card in the Active column is stalled (on the card). Active is the column.

board.stalled.notRunning.description: Why a card's work or review is stalled: its agent's session isn't running. {agent} is the agent's name.

board.stalled.notWatching.defaultMessage: {agent} isn't watching {card}: its turn ended with no card watch.
board.stalled.notWatching.description: Why a card in a card loop is stalled: the agent looping on it stopped without waiting for the card to change. {agent} is its name, {card} the card’s name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none. A card watch is what wakes an agent when a card changes.

board.stalled.removed.description: Why a card's work or review is stalled: its agent was removed from the project. {agent} is the agent's name.

board.stalled.removedUnnamed.description: Why a card's work is stalled: its agent (name unknown) was removed from the project.

board.stalled.reviewVerdictWait.defaultMessage: {agent} started reviewing {card} but has given no verdict, and has only been watching it for {waited}.
board.stalled.reviewVerdictWait.description: Why a card in Review is stalled: its reviewer started its review, then went back to waiting on the card without passing or failing it (it may have left a question in a comment). {agent} is the reviewer's name, {card} the card’s name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none, {waited} how long it has only been watching ("40 min", "2 h 5 min").

board.stalled.reviewWait.defaultMessage: {agent} is watching {card} but hasn't started reviewing it: in Review for {waited}.
board.stalled.reviewWait.description: Why a card waiting in Review is stalled: its reviewer watches it but hasn't started. {agent} is the reviewer's name, {card} the card’s name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none, {waited} how long it has waited ("40 min", "2 h 5 min").

board.stalled.reviewWaitBusy.defaultMessage: {agent} is watching {card} but hasn't started reviewing it (it is working on something else): in Review for {waited}.
board.stalled.reviewWaitBusy.description: Why a card waiting in Review is stalled: its reviewer watches it but is busy with other work. {agent} is the reviewer's name, {card} the card’s name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none, {waited} how long it has waited ("40 min", "2 h 5 min").

board.stalled.reviewWaitSilent.defaultMessage: {agent} is watching {card} but hasn't started reviewing it (it shows working, but has been silent for {silent}: state unknown): in Review for {waited}.
board.stalled.reviewWaitSilent.description: Why a card waiting in Review is stalled: its reviewer watches it but hasn't started, and Combwork can't tell what the reviewer is doing. {agent} is the reviewer's name, {card} the card’s name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none, {silent} minutes, {waited} how long it has waited ("40 min", "2 h 5 min"). {silent} is a duration too, written like {waited}.

board.stalled.startFailed.description: Why a card in the Active column is stalled: its agent couldn't be started. {agent} is the agent's name; {why} is the reason, in English as Combwork or the agent's CLI gave it.

board.stalled.startWaiting.description: Why a card in the Active column is stalled (HI-2304): Combwork can't start its agent in its slot yet, because the slot is held by processes a run left running there; it starts the agent once the slot is free. {agent} is the agent's name; {why} says what holds the slot, in English ("slot-a is held by WindowsSandboxServer, left running by MB1's last run").

board.stalled.wakeUntaken.defaultMessage: {agent} hasn't taken the wake Combwork typed for {card}: it waits in its prompt.
board.stalled.wakeUntaken.description: Why a card in a card loop is stalled: the agent watched the card, and Combwork typed its wake line into the agent's terminal, but the agent's CLI never sent it. {agent} is its name, {card} the card's name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none.

board.start.busy.description: Under a busy agent in the Start dialog, which can't take the card yet: what it is doing ({status}: "Working").

board.start.checkingConnection.defaultMessage: Finding out which coding agents are installed, to choose the first connection that can run…
board.start.checkingConnection.description: Under the new agent's choice of connection in the Start dialog (HI-2121) while Combwork still looks for the installed coding agent CLIs: the first usable connection is chosen once it knows; Start waits until then.

board.start.idle.defaultMessage: {status}: gets the card as its next message.
board.start.idle.description: Under an idle agent in the Start dialog: what it is doing ({status}: "Ready", "Finished"), and that the card is typed to it next.

board.start.intro.defaultMessage: The agent gets the card as its prompt (title and description), and the card moves to Active. A stopped agent starts a new conversation; an idle one gets it as its next message.
board.start.intro.description: At the top of the Start dialog. Active is a board column.

board.start.name.description: A field label in the Start dialog: the new agent's name.

board.start.namePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the new agent's name in the Start dialog: left empty, it is named Agent and a number.

board.start.newAgent.description: A choice in the Start dialog: the card starts on a new agent of the project.

board.start.newAgentText.defaultMessage: Works in the project folder, next to the others.
board.start.newAgentText.description: Under "A new agent" in the Start dialog.

board.start.noProject.description: Why a card can't start: it belongs to no project.

board.start.notGit.defaultMessage: The project is not a git repository.
board.start.notGit.description: Why a card cannot start on a new agent in its own worktree (the Start dialog): the project has no git repository.

board.start.ok.description: Button: closes the Start dialog of a card that has no project.

board.start.projectGone.defaultMessage: {project} isn't a project in this workspace.
board.start.projectGone.description: Why a card can't start: its project ({project}) isn't in the workspace.

board.start.providerOff.description: Under an agent in the Start dialog that can't take the card: its CLI ({provider}: Claude Code, Codex…) is turned off in Settings.

board.start.show.description: A button on the toast after a card started: shows the agent it started on.

board.start.started.description: A toast's title after a card started: its name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none and the agent ({agent}, its name). The card's title follows. A noun before the name (glossary §1 rule 4).

board.start.stopped.defaultMessage: Stopped: starts a new conversation on the card.
board.start.stopped.description: Under a stopped agent in the Start dialog: starting the card starts it with a new conversation.

board.start.title.description: Title of the Start dialog: the card’s name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none and title.

board.start.titleShort.description: Title of the Start dialog when the card can't start: {card} is its name: its key, such as AM-12, or #12 for a card with none.

board.start.worktreeAgent.defaultMessage: A new agent in its own worktree
board.start.worktreeAgent.description: A choice in the Start dialog: the card starts on a new agent with its own git worktree (branch and folder).

board.start.worktreeText.defaultMessage: Its own branch and folder; merge its work back when the card is done.
board.start.worktreeText.description: Under "A new agent in its own worktree" in the Start dialog.

board.strip.count.defaultMessage: {state, select, running {{n, plural, one {# running} other {# running}}} failed {{n, plural, one {# failed} other {# failed}}} stale {{n, plural, one {# stopped reporting} other {# stopped reporting}}} passed {{n, plural, one {# passed} other {# passed}}} other {{n, plural, one {# stopped} other {# stopped}}}}
board.strip.count.description: How many runs of the folded Progress strip are in a state ("3 running", "1 stopped reporting"), listed after its total ("8 runs: 3 running, 1 failed"). stale: stopped reporting.

board.strip.oneRun.defaultMessage: 1 run, {state, select, running {running} failed {failed} stale {stopped reporting} passed {passed} other {stopped}}
board.strip.oneRun.description: The folded Progress strip's name when it has one run, with that run's state (stale: it stopped reporting).

board.strip.runs.description: The folded Progress strip's name: how many runs, then how many are in each state ("8 runs: 5 running, 2 failed"). {states} is that list.

board.target.failed.defaultMessage: Where the card merges wasn’t changed
board.target.failed.description: HI-2556: an error toast’s title: setting a card’s Merges into failed. Its text says why.

board.target.field.description: HI-2556: a field label in the card dialog: the branch the card’s work is made from and merges into (Darren’s name for it).

board.target.mark.description: HI-2556: a mark on a card’s tile: its work merges into {branch} (a branch name), not the project’s Work merges into.

board.target.markTip.defaultMessage: This card’s work is made from {branch} and merges into it, not the project’s Work merges into.
board.target.markTip.description: HI-2556: tooltip and accessible name of a card tile’s Merges into mark. {branch} is a branch name.

board.target.own.description: HI-2556: the first choice of the card dialog’s Merges into: the project’s Work merges into, {branch} its name.

board.team.cw.description: Who runs something while the team is paused when no agent does (HI-2081): Combwork itself (a slot's setup, a merge). Combwork is the product's name.

board.team.endDetail.defaultMessage: Only that process and what it started end, and only while they are still the ones listed. Work they had not saved is lost.
board.team.endDetail.description: Detail of the question before ending a process from the paused team's band (HI-2081).

board.team.endFailed.description: A notice (HI-2081): ending a process from the paused team’s band failed, or it was no longer the one listed. {label} is what it runs.

board.team.endIt.description: A button beside a process the paused team's band names (HI-2081): ends it and what it started, after a question (…).

board.team.endMessage.description: The question before ending a process (HI-2081). {agent} is the agent's name, {label} what the process runs, {pid} its id.

board.team.endTitle.description: Title of the question before ending a process the paused team's band names (HI-2081).

board.team.install.description: A button on the paused team’s band (HI-2081), once all are parked and an update is ready: restarts Combwork and installs the update (checked again first).

board.team.item.defaultMessage: {kind, select, working {{agent} is working} starting {{agent} is starting} background {{agent} has background tasks running} run {{agent}: {label} (a run)} merge {A merge: {label}} copy {A check in a copy: {label}} process {{agent}: {label} (process {pid})} writer {{agent}: its slot {label} is still held} status {{agent}: Combwork can’t tell what it is doing} other {{agent}: can’t be checked now}}
board.team.item.description: One thing that still runs while the team is paused (HI-2081), a line in its band. {agent} is an agent's name (or Assistant); {label} the user's own words for it (a run's title, a process's command, a slot's name); {pid} a process id. kind: working or starting; background tasks; a run (a test run through cw-progress); a merge of the merge queue; a check in a copy (a folder Combwork keeps at one revision); a process (a test runner, a dev server, a test copy of Combwork); its slot (a working folder Combwork lends) still held by its processes; its state unknown; or (other) its processes can't be read now. Keep the select keys.

board.team.notParked.defaultMessage: The team isn't parked any more, so the update wasn't installed.
board.team.notParked.description: A notice (HI-2081): the user chose Install Now, and as Combwork checked again something had started running (an agent, a run) in an open workspace.

board.team.otherNotPaused.description: A line in the paused team's band (HI-2081): another open workspace ({name}, its folder's name) isn't paused, so the update can't be installed yet.

board.team.parked.description: The band in the Progress panel's Lanes (HI-2081): the team is paused and nothing runs in any open workspace, so an update can be installed.

board.team.pause.description: A button and command (the Progress panel's Lanes, the command palette, Help → Check for Updates) (HI-2081): before an update, Combwork starts no lane card, wakes no agent with card events and gives no reviews out in every open workspace, and tells each running agent once to finish its turn, end its runs and commit. 'The team' is every agent of the workspace.

board.team.pauseFailed.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {# workspace couldn't be paused: {names}} other {# workspaces couldn't be paused: {names}}}
board.team.pauseFailed.description: A notice (HI-2081): Pause the Team could not save the pause of some open workspaces (their folder names in {names}); they are not held, and the app is never shown as parked while one is not.

board.team.pauseFirst.description: A button in Help → Check for Updates, when an update is ready and agents are running (HI-2081): pauses the team (see Pause the Team) so it can be installed once every agent has parked.

board.team.pausing.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {Pausing the team: # still running} other {Pausing the team: # still running}}
board.team.pausing.description: The band in the Progress panel's Lanes while the team is paused (HI-2081) and not every agent has parked yet: n things still run (agents working, runs, processes), listed below.

board.team.resume.description: A button and command (HI-2081): lifts the pause of every open workspace, so lanes start their cards and agents are woken again.

board.team.showWindow.description: A button beside another open workspace's name in the paused team's band (HI-2095): brings forward the Combwork window showing that workspace, where what still runs in it can be ended.

board.team.showWindowTitle.defaultMessage: Its processes are ended from its own window
board.team.showWindowTitle.description: The tooltip of Show Its Window in the paused team's band (HI-2095): End It is offered only in the window of the workspace a process belongs to.

board.team.thisWorkspace.description: A heading in the paused team's band, over what still runs in the window's own workspace (HI-2081), when several are open.

board.team.windowGone.defaultMessage: {name} isn’t open in a window any more
board.team.windowGone.description: A notice (HI-2095): the user chose Show Its Window for another workspace ({name}, its folder's name) in the paused team's band, but no window shows it now.

board.toolbar.archived.description: A checkbox in the board's toolbar: shows the archived cards instead (how many there are: {n}).

board.toolbar.forYou.description: A checkbox in the board's toolbar: shows only the cards something waits on the user for (an approval, a decision, a question), and how many there are ({n}). Glossary: For you.

board.toolbar.more.description: Tooltip on the board toolbar's ⋯ button: opens the board's menu (Archive All Cards…).

board.toolbar.search.description: Placeholder of the board's search box: finds cards by name (AM-12: a project key, a hyphen and a number; AM- finds all of that project's; #12 works too), words or labels.

board.toolbar.startLane.description: An item of the board's ⋯ menu: opens Start Lane (a builder and a reviewer agent work through cards in turn). Glossary: lane.

board.upgrade.askDetail.defaultMessage: Close every other Combwork that has this workspace open first. Until it is upgraded, its board is read-only here and its agents can't start.
board.upgrade.askDetail.description: Under the upgrade dialog's text: the upgrade is refused while another copy of Combwork has the workspace open; declining leaves the board readable but not changeable in this Combwork, and no agent (nor the Assistant) can start.

board.upgrade.askMessage.defaultMessage: Combwork 1.0 needs to upgrade this workspace's data. Version 0.9 can then no longer open it; a backup of the board is kept, and Help → Restore the 0.9 Board Backup… puts it back. Back up first: there's no going back to 0.9.3 once your agents' worktrees become slots.
board.upgrade.askMessage.description: The upgrade dialog's text: why (1.0 keeps the workspace's data in a new format), then what follows: version 0.9 can't open the board any more, and a copy of the board as it was is kept; but the agents' own worktrees become slots (working folders Combwork lends to cards), which 0.9.3 can't use again, so the user should back up first. Help → Restore the 0.9 Board Backup… is a command in the Help menu: keep its name as Combwork shows it. Keep 0.9.3 as it is (a version).

board.upgrade.askTitle.description: Title of the dialog Combwork shows on opening a workspace whose task board was saved by version 0.9: 1.0 keeps the board in a new format, and asks before converting it.

board.upgrade.banner.defaultMessage: This workspace is from version 0.9: until it is upgraded to 1.0, its board is read-only here and its agents can't start.
board.upgrade.banner.description: A banner at the top of the window while the workspace's upgrade to 1.0's format waits (the user said Not Now): cards can be read but not changed, and no agent (nor the Assistant) can start, as Combwork couldn't record its session. Also the tooltip of what is disabled meanwhile: the board's add-card buttons, dragging cards, the card dialog's changes, and New Session and Resume.

board.upgrade.bannerButton.description: A button on the banner above a read-only 0.9 board: asks to upgrade it to 1.0. The … says it asks first: keep it.

board.upgrade.done.description: A notification after the workspace's board was converted to 1.0's format.

board.upgrade.doneDetail.defaultMessage: The 0.9 board is kept: Help → Restore the 0.9 Board Backup… puts it back.
board.upgrade.doneDetail.description: Under "Board upgraded to 1.0". Help → Restore the 0.9 Board Backup… is a command in the Help menu: keep its name as Combwork shows it.

board.upgrade.learnMore.description: A button on the banner above a read-only 0.9 board: opens the user guide's section about upgrading to 1.0.

board.upgrade.notNow.description: The upgrade dialog's other button: leaves the board as it is, read-only in this Combwork, with a banner offering the upgrade.

board.upgrade.upgrade.description: The upgrade dialog's button: converts the board to 1.0's format.

board.upgrade.upgrading.description: The Upgrade button while the board is converted.

board.view.intro.defaultMessage: Plan work as cards, start them on agents, and see where each one is on its way to Done.
board.view.intro.description: Under the Task Board's title, whatever the workflow (HI-2341: some have no Review or Approved). Done is the board's last column, in every workflow.

board.view.noWorkspace.defaultMessage: Open a workspace to see its task board.
board.view.noWorkspace.description: The Task Board view with no workspace open.

board.view.title.description: The board's name: the title of the Task Board view and of its sidebar.

board.view.workspaceCards.description: After the Task Board's title when the sidebar shows the cards of no project (about the whole workspace). Lower case.

board.work.accepted.description: The card dialog's Work section: the card's work was accepted (a project without version control, or a no-code card) at {when}, a date and time.

board.work.adopted.defaultMessage: Adopted at the upgrade, from {column}: its work starts from what its folder showed then.
board.work.adopted.description: The card dialog's Work section for a card Combwork took on at the upgrade to 1.0 from what could be read. {column} is the board column it was in (Doing, Review, Passed).

board.work.backAtApproved.defaultMessage: Its branch came back to {revision}, the revision that passed: the pass counts again.
board.work.backAtApproved.description: A mark in the card dialog's Work section: the card's branch changed after its pass (which made the pass stale), then came back to exactly the revision that passed ({revision}, a short commit id), so the pass counts again. Glossary: pass, revision.

board.work.badgeOutside.description: Tooltip and accessible name of a mark on a board card: the card was merged by hand before its rules passed. Glossary: rule.

board.work.badgeOverride.defaultMessage: {by, select, assistant {The Assistant moved it past its rules} other {You moved it past its rules}}: {rules}. {hasReason, select, yes {Reason: {reason}} other {No reason given.}}
board.work.badgeOverride.description: Tooltip and accessible name of a mark on a board card (and a line in its lane segment's hover): a move made an exception to the card's workflow rules (glossary: override), by the user (other) or the Combwork Assistant (assistant) (select: translate each); {rules} lists the rules it skipped (their names); then the reason the user or the Assistant gave (their own words), or that none was given. Glossary: rule, override.

board.work.badgeStale.defaultMessage: Stale: its pass no longer counts for its revision
board.work.badgeStale.description: Tooltip and accessible name of a mark on a board card: the card's pass is stale (for an older revision, or before a decision). Glossary: stale.

board.work.base.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the revision the card's work started from follows (a short commit id, a3f2c1d).

board.work.branch.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the git branch the card's work is on follows.

board.work.carriedOver.defaultMessage: The pass for {from} carries over to {to}: the same change.
board.work.carriedOver.description: A mark in the card dialog's Work section: a pass for an earlier revision ({from}) still counts for a later one ({to}) with exactly the same changes. Glossary: carries over, same change.

board.work.check.defaultMessage: {name}: {result, select, passed {passed} failed {failed} other {stopped}}{counted, select, no { (not counted)} other {}}
board.work.check.description: A check under a revision in the card dialog's Work section: its name (typecheck, as the project names it), then a colon and how it ended; (not counted) when it doesn't count for the revision (its hover says why). Keep the select keys. Glossary: check.

board.work.failed.description: The card dialog's Work section when its work couldn't be read (the repository or the board). {error} is why, in the words of the error.

board.work.files.defaultMessage: {n, plural, =0 {No files changed} one {# file changed} other {# files changed}}
board.work.files.description: A button in the card dialog's Work section: how many files the revision changed; a click shows them.

board.work.filesNotRead.defaultMessage: {note, select, beforeChange {Files not read} noBaseOrHead {Files not read: there was no base or revision to compare} other {Files not read: Combwork couldn't read {why}}}
board.work.filesNotRead.description: In the card dialog's Work section, in place of a revision's changed files: Combwork couldn't read which files changed when it was submitted. {note} picks why: Combwork read nothing then (beforeChange: the revision's line above says why), it had no base or revision to compare (noBaseOrHead), or another reason, {why}: what it couldn't read (already translated). Keep the select keys. Glossary: revision.

board.work.folder.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the folder the card's work is done in follows (the project folder, or its own folder).

board.work.folderGone.defaultMessage: Its folder, {folder}, is no longer an agent’s worktree: its files can’t be opened here.
board.work.folderGone.description: Under a revision's files in the card dialog's Work section: the folder the work was done in ({folder}, a path) isn't any agent's worktree now, so its files aren't opened in another folder instead.

board.work.integrated.defaultMessage: {method, select, merge {Merged into {target} as {result}} squash {Squashed into {target} as {result}} fastForward {{target} moved forward to {result}} sameTree {Already in {target} at {result}} other {Committed in {target} as {result}}}
board.work.integrated.description: The card dialog's Work section: how the card's work went into its target ({target}, a branch such as main) and the target's revision with it ({result}, a short commit id). Keep the select keys.

board.work.leftTarget.defaultMessage: No longer in {target}: its revision {revision} was taken out.
board.work.leftTarget.description: A mark in the card dialog's Work section: a Done card's revision ({revision}, a short commit id) is no longer in its target ({target}, a branch such as main).

board.work.mergedInPart.defaultMessage: Merged in part: some of its work is already in {target}.
board.work.mergedInPart.description: A mark in the card dialog's Work section: part of the unfinished card's work was found in its target ({target}, a branch such as main).

board.work.noCode.description: In place of a revision in the card dialog's Work section: a no-code card's submission (design, investigation), which has no revision. Glossary: no-code card.

board.work.noRecord.defaultMessage: No work record: its board isn’t upgraded to Combwork 1.0, or the card has no project.
board.work.noRecord.description: The card dialog's Work section when there is no work to show: the board hasn't had the 1.0 upgrade, or the card is the workspace's (no project).

board.work.noRevision.description: In place of a revision in the card dialog's Work section: the card's revision couldn't be read when it was submitted (a project without version control, before Combwork reads its revisions). Glossary: revision.

board.work.none.description: The card dialog's Work section for a card whose builder hasn't submitted a revision for review yet. Glossary: revision.

board.work.notRead.defaultMessage: {note, select, beforeChange {Not read when its work started} noTarget {Not read: there was no target branch to start from} other {Combwork couldn't read {why}}}
board.work.notRead.description: In the card dialog's Work section, in place of a branch, base or target Combwork couldn't read when the card's work started. {note} picks why: Combwork read nothing as the work started (beforeChange), it had no target branch to find the base from (noTarget), or another reason, {why}: what Combwork couldn't read (such as "the latest commit in …", already translated). Keep the select keys. Glossary: target branch.

board.work.openFile.description: Tooltip of a file a revision changed (card dialog's Work section): opens it in the project's Files tab. {path} is the file's path.

board.work.outsideCombwork.description: The card dialog's Work section, under how the card was merged: the merge was made outside Combwork (in a terminal or another tool). Glossary: outside Combwork.

board.work.outsideRules.description: A mark in the card dialog's Work section: the card was merged by hand before these rules passed ({rules}, the rules' names, joined). Glossary: rule.

board.work.overridden.defaultMessage: Moved past its review and approvals by an override.
board.work.overridden.description: A mark in the card dialog's Work section: the card's latest revision was moved on by an override (the user's or the Assistant's exception to the rules). Glossary: override.

board.work.preWorkflow.defaultMessage: Before 1.0: this card has no work record.
board.work.preWorkflow.description: The card dialog's Work section for a card from before 1.0: Combwork records no work for it and invents none. Glossary: before 1.0.

board.work.projectFolder.description: The card dialog's Work section, after Folder: the card's work is done in the project's own folder (not a folder of its own).

board.work.reading.description: The card dialog's Work section while the card's work is being read.

board.work.retry.description: A button in the card dialog's Work section after its work couldn't be read: reads it again.

board.work.revisionNotRead.defaultMessage: {note, select, beforeChange {No revision recorded: Combwork didn't read one when the card went to Review.} other {Revision not read when it was submitted: Combwork couldn't read {why}.}} Its next submission reads it again.
board.work.revisionNotRead.description: In place of a revision in the card dialog's Work section. {note} picks why: Combwork read nothing when the card was moved into Review (beforeChange; the card had no agent then, say), or it couldn't read the revision when the builder submitted it, {why}: what it couldn't read (such as "the latest commit in …", already translated). Then: the next submission reads it again. Keep the select keys. Glossary: revision.

board.work.revisions.description: A heading in the card dialog's Work section, above the revisions the builder submitted for review. Glossary: revision.

board.work.round.description: Beside a revision in the card dialog's Work section: the review round it was submitted in (1, 2…).

board.work.staleChange.defaultMessage: Stale: the pass was for {approved}; the card is now at {current}.
board.work.staleChange.description: A mark in the card dialog's Work section: the card's pass is for an older revision ({approved}, a short commit id) that isn't the same change as its revision now ({current}). Glossary: stale, pass.

board.work.staleDecision.defaultMessage: Stale: a decision was recorded since the pass.
board.work.staleDecision.description: A mark in the card dialog's Work section: the card's pass no longer counts because the user recorded a decision on the card after it. Glossary: stale, pass.

board.work.staleNext.defaultMessage: To move it on, its builder submits it again, or puts its branch back at {approved}: until then it isn’t merged.
board.work.staleNext.description: A mark in the card dialog's Work section under a stale pass, in Approved (Passed): what moves the card on. Its builder submits its work again (for a new review), or puts its branch back at the revision that passed ({approved}, a short commit id), which makes the pass count again. Glossary: stale, pass.

board.work.target.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: where the card's work goes once approved follows (the target branch, main). Glossary: target branch.

board.work.title.description: A heading in the card dialog (click to show or hide): what the card's facts say of its work (its branch, revisions, verdicts, checks, merge). Glossary: work.

board.work.verdict.defaultMessage: {reviewer}: {pass, select, yes {passed} other {failed}}{current, select, no { (no longer counts)} other {}}
board.work.verdict.description: A verdict under a revision in the card dialog's Work section: who reviewed it ({reviewer}, an agent's name, then a colon) and whether it passed or failed; (no longer counts) when a newer revision or decision came since. Keep the select keys. Glossary: verdict, pass/fail.

board.workQueue.advance.defaultMessage: Tested and ready: update {target} in its folder now?
board.workQueue.advance.description: The card dialog's Work section: the merge queue waits for the user's OK before it updates the branch {target}, which is checked out in a folder (its files change there). The same question waits under For you.

board.workQueue.advancing.description: The card dialog's Work section: the merge queue is moving the branch {target} to the card's merged result now.

board.workQueue.answerFailed.description: An error's title: approving or declining the update of a checked-out branch failed (the card dialog).

board.workQueue.approve.description: A button in the card dialog's Work section: the user's OK to update the checked-out branch now (the same answer as under For you). Glossary 2.3: Approve.

board.workQueue.approved.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section's merge queue part: the revision that was approved and is merged follows (a short commit id). Glossary: revision.

board.workQueue.cancelled.defaultMessage: {reason, select, removed {Taken out of the queue (Remove from queue).} stale {Taken out of the queue: its pass no longer counts.} hold {Taken out of the queue: the card went On Hold.} decision {Taken out of the queue: a decision was recorded.} integratedOutside {Taken out of the queue: it was merged outside Combwork.} followUp {Taken out of the queue for a follow-up: queued again once its reviewer checks it.} other {Taken out of the queue.}}
board.workQueue.cancelled.description: The card dialog's Work section: the card's merge queue entry was cancelled, and why. Keep the select keys. Glossary: merge queue, On Hold, decision, outside Combwork, follow-up.

board.workQueue.command.defaultMessage: {purpose, select, finish {To finish it} other {To undo it}}, in {folder}
board.workQueue.command.description: Above a command in the card dialog's Work section: what it does (finish or undo the stopped merge) and the folder to run it in ({folder}: its name, such as alpha; the full path on hover). Keep the select keys.

board.workQueue.commands.defaultMessage: Commands (PowerShell): nothing runs them for you
board.workQueue.commands.description: A sub-heading in the card dialog's Work section, over the git commands that finish or undo a stopped merge: the user runs them in PowerShell; Combwork doesn't.

board.workQueue.conflictFiles.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the files the merge conflicted in follow.

board.workQueue.copied.description: A notification after copying a command from the card dialog's Work section.

board.workQueue.copy.description: A button beside a command in the card dialog's Work section: copies it. Keep it short.

board.workQueue.copyFailed.description: A notification: copying a command from the card dialog's Work section failed.

board.workQueue.copyNamed.defaultMessage: Copy the command {purpose, select, finish {to finish it} other {to undo it}}
board.workQueue.copyNamed.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside a command in the card dialog's Work section. Keep the select keys.

board.workQueue.decline.description: A button in the card dialog's Work section: declines updating the checked-out branch now, asking why first (…; the same answer as under For you).

board.workQueue.declineNeeds.description: An error in the question when the user declines the merge queue's update of a checked-out branch without a reason: one is needed.

board.workQueue.declineTitle.description: Title of the question when the user declines the merge queue's update of the checked-out branch {target} (the card dialog's Work section): their reason follows.

board.workQueue.declineWhy.defaultMessage: Why? Your reason is added to the card as your comment.
board.workQueue.declineWhy.description: The question when the user declines the merge queue's update of a checked-out branch (the card dialog's Work section): their reason, recorded on the card as their comment.

board.workQueue.expected.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the commit the branch was at before the merge follows.

board.workQueue.files.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {# file, and where it is} other {# files, and where each is}}
board.workQueue.files.description: A sub-heading in the card dialog's Work section, over the files a stopped merge left: how many ({n}), and for each whether it is as before the merge, as merged, or neither.

board.workQueue.heading.description: A sub-heading in the card dialog's Work section: where the card stands in the merge queue follows. Glossary 2.5: merge queue.

board.workQueue.hideLog.description: A button in the card dialog's Work section: hides a return's whole output shown above it.

board.workQueue.noBranch.description: In the card dialog's Work section, after Its branch: the folder isn't on any branch. HEAD is git's: keep it.

board.workQueue.noCommands.defaultMessage: Its files are neither as they were nor as merged: put them right by hand.
board.workQueue.noCommands.description: In the card dialog's Work section when no command can settle a stopped merge: the user fixes the files by hand.

board.workQueue.output.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {Its output’s last line} other {Its output’s last # lines}}
board.workQueue.output.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the last lines ({n}) of what the failed check or hook printed follow.

board.workQueue.paused.description: A heading line in the card dialog's Work section: the merge queue for the branch {target} is paused (why follows).

board.workQueue.queued.defaultMessage: Queued for {target}: {position, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}} in line
board.workQueue.queued.description: The card dialog's Work section: the card waits in the merge queue for the branch {target}, at place {position} (1st: next; the card testing now counts). Glossary 2.5: merge queue.

board.workQueue.queuedNoPlace.description: The card dialog's Work section: the card waits in the merge queue for the branch {target} (its place isn't known here: another Combwork runs the queue).

board.workQueue.result.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the merged commit follows.

board.workQueue.retried.description: The card dialog's Work section: the card's revision was queued again, unchanged, by the user's Retry merge.

board.workQueue.retry.description: A button in the card dialog's Work section on a card the merge queue returned: queues its approved revision again, unchanged (asks first).

board.workQueue.retryApprovedMessage.defaultMessage: This queues {revision} again, unchanged: the revision that was approved, not a new one.
board.workQueue.retryApprovedMessage.description: The confirmation before Retry merge on a card taken out of the merge queue and still approved (in Approved): the same approved revision ({revision}, a short commit id) goes back into the queue. Unlike after a return, there's no once-per-revision limit here. Glossary: revision.

board.workQueue.retryConfirm.description: The button confirming Retry merge. Keep it short.

board.workQueue.retryFailed.description: An error's title: Retry merge failed (the card dialog); its message says why.

board.workQueue.retryMessage.defaultMessage: This queues {revision} again, unchanged: the revision that was approved, not a new one. Once per revision.
board.workQueue.retryMessage.description: The confirmation before Retry merge: the same approved revision ({revision}, a short commit id) goes back into the merge queue; it can be done once per revision. Glossary: revision.

board.workQueue.retryTitle.description: Title of the confirmation before Retry merge ({card}: the card's key).

board.workQueue.retryUsed.defaultMessage: Retry merge was used for this revision: a new revision goes to the queue once it is submitted and passes review.
board.workQueue.retryUsed.description: The card dialog's Work section, on a card the merge queue returned after a Retry merge: Retry merge works once per revision, so it isn't offered again; the next way back into the queue is a new revision through review. Glossary: revision.

board.workQueue.retryWaits.defaultMessage: {step, select, followUp {Retry merge comes back once its reviewer has checked the follow-up.} other {Retry merge comes back once its reviewer has checked the design.}}
board.workQueue.retryWaits.description: The card dialog's Work section, on a card taken out of the merge queue while a card loop's step waits for its reviewer (a follow-up of reviewed work, or a design): Retry merge isn't offered until the reviewer answers it. Keep the select keys. Glossary: follow-up, design.

board.workQueue.returned.description: The card dialog's Work section: the merge queue returned the card to its builder ({when}: how long ago), and why ({why}: conflict in tasks.ts, checks failed: unit, a hook failed…). Glossary 2.4: returned.

board.workQueue.showRun.description: A button in the card dialog's Work section: shows the merge check running now in the Progress panel's Runs tab.

board.workQueue.side.defaultMessage: {side, select, expected {as before the merge} result {as merged} other {neither}}
board.workQueue.side.description: Beside a file in the card dialog's Work section: whether its contents are as before the merge, as merged, or neither. Keep the select keys.

board.workQueue.stuck.defaultMessage: Its merge into {target} stopped part way. Combwork changes nothing more on its own: put it right with one of the commands below, then answer under For you.
board.workQueue.stuck.description: The card dialog's Work section: the merge queue's update of the checked-out branch {target} stopped half done (a crash, another program); the user settles it by hand. For you: where the card's request waits (glossary 2.3).

board.workQueue.stuckBranch.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the branch that folder is on now follows (or that it is on none).

board.workQueue.stuckFolder.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the folder the target is checked out in follows (a path).

board.workQueue.stuckRef.description: A label in the card dialog's Work section: the commit the branch {target} points at now follows.

board.workQueue.testing.description: The card dialog's Work section: the merge queue is testing the card now, at a step ({step}: test merge, merge checks, check: unit, merging into main). Glossary 2.5: merge queue.

board.workQueue.unreadRef.description: In the card dialog's Work section: where the branch points couldn't be read.

board.workflows.description: A button in the board's toolbar when it shows several projects: opens a list of each project's workflow (glossary 2.1: workflow), each opening that project's Version Control tab.
